/-!
# Whitehead conjecture

The Whitehead conjecture (also called the Whitehead asphericity conjecture) was formulated by
J. H. C. Whitehead in 1941. It states that every connected subcomplex of a two-dimensional
aspherical CW complex is aspherical.

A space $Y$ is *aspherical* if it is connected and all of its higher homotopy groups vanish, i.e.
$\pi_n(Y) = 0$ for all $n \ge 2$. For a CW complex this is equivalent to the universal cover
being contractible.

A CW complex is modelled as a closed subset `C` of a Hausdorff space `X` equipped with a CW
structure `Topology.CWComplex C`. It is two-dimensional if it has no cells of dimension
greater than $2$. A subcomplex is a `Topology.CWComplex.Subcomplex C`, i.e. a closed subset of
`C` that is a union of open cells of `C`; it is not assumed to be finite.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitehead_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- J. H. C. Whitehead, *On adding relations to homotopy groups*, Annals of Mathematics 42 (1941),
  409–428. [doi:10.2307/1968907](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968907)
-/

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop: for every CW complex X of dimension ≤ 2 that is aspherical (connected with π_n(X)=0 for all n≥2, equivalently contractible universal cover) and every connected subcomplex L ⊆ X (not assumed finite), L is aspherical; the article's equivalent form via aspherical group presentations (π_2(K(S|R))=0 for sub-presentations) and the Bestvina–Brady dichotomy with Eilenberg–Ganea are background only, not separately posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c07 is a faithful rendering: Mathlib's classical `Topology.CWComplex C` on a Hausdorff ambient space (`T2Space X` is required because Mathlib's class deliberately admits non-Hausdorff spaces, whereas CW complexes in the conjecture are Hausdorff), dimension ≤ 2 as `∀ n, 2 < n → IsEmpty (cell C n)`, aspherical = connected + `Subsingleton (π_ n Y y)` for all n ≥ 2 and all basepoints (π_n is a nonempty quotient so Subsingleton is exactly triviality), arbitrary non-finite `Subcomplex C`, and the literal hypothesis `IsConnected (E : Set X)` (which includes nonemptiness, excluding the empty subcomplex). Edited only to make the bespoke class `extends ConnectedSpace` in Mathlib style and to adjust the test proof accordingly. c02/c08 were equally faithful (path-connected variants, equivalent for CW complexes); c04/c05 fine but use `C = univ`; c03 uses PathConnectedSpace for the hypothesis (less literal); c06 has non-conventional extra Mathlib imports; c01 omits `T2Space`, so it ranges over Mathlib's strictly larger non-Hausdorff 'CW complexes' and is not faithful as written.

context:
The Whitehead conjecture (also known as the Whitehead asphericity conjecture) is a claim in algebraic topology. It was formulated by J. H. C. Whitehead in 1941. It states that every connected subcomplex of a two-dimensional aspherical CW complex is aspherical.
A group presentation $G=(S\mid R)$ is called aspherical if the two-dimensional CW complex $K(S\mid R)$ associated with this presentation is aspherical or, equivalently, if $\pi _{2}(K(S\mid R))=0$. The Whitehead conjecture is equivalent to the conjecture that every sub-presentation of an aspherical presentation is aspherical.
In 1997, Mladen Bestvina and Noel Brady constructed a group G so that either G is a counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture, or there must be a counterexample to the Whitehead conjecture; in other words, it is not possible for both conjectures to be true.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct; the equivalent presentation-theoretic form and the Bestvina–Brady/Eilenberg–Ganea dichotomy are background only and were not formalized.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Whitehead conjecture

The Whitehead conjecture (also called the Whitehead asphericity conjecture) was formulated by
J. H. C. Whitehead in 1941. It states that every connected subcomplex of a two-dimensional
aspherical CW complex is aspherical.

A space $Y$ is *aspherical* if it is connected and all of its higher homotopy groups vanish, i.e.
$\pi_n(Y) = 0$ for all $n \ge 2$. For a CW complex this is equivalent to the universal cover
being contractible.

A CW complex is modelled as a closed subset `C` of a Hausdorff space `X` equipped with a CW
structure `Topology.CWComplex C`. It is two-dimensional if it has no cells of dimension
greater than $2$. A subcomplex is a `Topology.CWComplex.Subcomplex C`, i.e. a closed subset of
`C` that is a union of open cells of `C`; it is not assumed to be finite.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitehead_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- J. H. C. Whitehead, *On adding relations to homotopy groups*, Annals of Mathematics 42 (1941),
  409–428. [doi:10.2307/1968907](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968907)
-/

open Topology

namespace WhiteheadConjecture

/-- A topological space `Y` is *aspherical* if it is connected and all of its higher homotopy
groups vanish: $\pi_n(Y, y) = 0$ for every $n \ge 2$ and every base point $y \in Y$. -/
class AsphericalSpace (Y : Type*) [TopologicalSpace Y] : Prop extends ConnectedSpace Y where
  subsingleton_homotopyGroup : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∀ y : Y, Subsingleton (π_ n Y y)

/-- A one-point space is aspherical. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
instance : AsphericalSpace Unit where
  subsingleton_homotopyGroup _ _ _ := Quot.Subsingleton

/-- A disconnected space is not aspherical. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem not_asphericalSpace_bool : ¬ AsphericalSpace Bool := by
  intro h
  exact Bool.false_ne_true (h.toConnectedSpace.toPreconnectedSpace.constant continuous_id)

/--
**Whitehead conjecture.** Every connected subcomplex of a two-dimensional aspherical CW complex
is aspherical.

Here `C` is a CW complex (a closed subset of a Hausdorff space `X` with a CW structure) that is
two-dimensional (no cells of dimension $n > 2$) and aspherical, and `E` is a connected subcomplex
of `C`. The subcomplex `E` is not assumed to be finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 55 57]
theorem whitehead_conjecture {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] (C : Set X)
    [CWComplex C] (hdim : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 < n → IsEmpty (RelCWComplex.cell C n)) [AsphericalSpace C]
    (E : CWComplex.Subcomplex C) (hE : IsConnected (E : Set X)) :
    AsphericalSpace (E : Set X) := by
  sorry

end WhiteheadConjecture

items: "Two-dimensional" is modelled as dimension ≤ 2 (`∀ n, 2 < n → IsEmpty (RelCWComplex.cell C n)`), following the standard meaning of "2-complex" in this literature and the decomposition note; the case of dimension ≤ 1 (graphs) is a known theorem, so this is equivalent to requiring dimension exactly 2.

"Aspherical" is modelled as `ConnectedSpace Y ∧ ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ y, Subsingleton (π_ n Y y)`, i.e. connected with all higher homotopy groups trivial at every base point (for a connected CW complex, base-point independence makes the ∀ over base points harmless). The equivalent "contractible universal cover" formulation was not used since Mathlib lacks universal covers. Connectedness of the ambient complex is included in the aspherical hypothesis (standard convention); the conjecture with or without ambient connectedness is equivalent because a connected subcomplex lies in a single component.

CW complexes are modelled with Mathlib's classical `Topology.CWComplex C` for `C : Set X`, with the extra hypothesis `[T2Space X]`. This is essential: without Hausdorffness Mathlib's class admits non-CW spaces (e.g. the indiscrete two-point space with two 0-cells satisfies `closed'` vacuously). Every genuine CW complex is Hausdorff and can be realised as `C = Set.univ` in itself, so no generality is lost. Mathlib's `Subcomplex` instance for CW complexes also requires `T2Space X`.

"Connected subcomplex" is modelled as `E : CWComplex.Subcomplex C` (closed subset that is a union of open cells, matching Hatcher's definition) with `IsConnected (E : Set X)` (topological connectedness; for CW complexes this coincides with path-connectedness). The subcomplex is not assumed finite.
Homotopy groups are Mathlib's `HomotopyGroup.Pi` (`π_ n Y y`); triviality of the group is expressed as `Subsingleton`, which is correct since the type is nonempty (it is a group for n ≥ 1).

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; all eight candidates compiled and formalized it with the same overall shape. Main faithfulness discriminator: `T2Space X` (needed; Mathlib's `CWComplex` `closed'` axiom is one-directional and does not force Hausdorffness, e.g. an indiscrete two-point space with two 0-cells is a Mathlib CWComplex). 'Two-dimensional' is read as dimension ≤ 2 per the decomposition notes; the dimension ≤ 1 case is classical, so this is equivalent to the exact-dimension-2 reading. Connected vs path-connected in the definition of aspherical and in the subcomplex hypothesis are equivalent for CW complexes; the final file uses `ConnectedSpace`/`IsConnected` literally. Basepoint quantification is harmless for connected CW complexes. No finiteness assumption on complex or subcomplex. The presentation-theoretic equivalent and the Bestvina–Brady dichotomy are background only and not stated. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
statement: Whitehead conjecture: every connected subcomplex of a two-dimensional aspherical CW complex is aspherical.
